(c) No safety risk arises merely because administrative work is handled by another RFSIC; and  
(d) This practice is **not implemented to bypass any FSD requirements**.

28. I further believe this practice **is recognised by the FSD**. On the FSD’s website, there is a table setting out guidance as to which class of RFSIC should be engaged for different types of fire service systems, installations and equipment (the screenshot of that website (both Chinese and English version) made on 31 March 2026 was at **Annexure-3**¹).

29. By way of illustration, the table indicates that for a dust detection system, a Class 1 RFSIC should be engaged, while for emergency lighting, a Class 2 RFSIC should be engaged. However, the same table also shows that for a number of fire service systems and equipment, no class of RFSIC is specified as appropriate. These include fire control centre, fireman’s lift, firefighting and rescue stairway, and, most importantly for the present case, **supply tank**.

30. Using supply tank as an example, repair works to a supply tank (供水缸) will necessarily affect the fire hydrant and hose reel system, and therefore a SDN must be applied for. However, since no class of RFSIC is identified as appropriate for carrying out repair works to a supply tank, such works must in practice be carried out **by another company**, whether by way of subcontracting or other arrangement.

31. In those circumstances, it is my understanding that the **FSD has accepted**, or indeed expected, that the RFSIC signing the SDN application **may not necessarily be the same company carrying out the actual works**. Likewise, I believe it is appropriate for different companies to be involved in different roles, namely signing the SDN application, carrying out inspection of the fire service systems, and performing the actual works.
